tldr: A loose research cluster, not one event: it opened Oct 22 with DoorDash's multi-agent flag cleanup and a paper on herding cascades, then widened into agent benchmarks, training, orchestration and memory papers. From Nov 1 several papers questioned the evals themselves: task depth, non-English tool use, LLM-judge drift and single-run variance.
whats_new: JioHotstar benchmarked 6 code-retrieval approaches for AI coding agents on SWE, CodeScale Bench and an internal Q&A harness, finding structural search performed well on concrete tasks.
why_it_matters: An agent's score depends on the eval design and on what retrieval puts in its context, and this thread now has evidence on both from production teams, not only from papers.

beats.headline: Multi-agent systems meet production: write-ups and failure modes
beats.summary: Industry case studies sit next to a paper showing agents herding into runaway cascades.

beats.headline: Long-horizon agents get exam-style benchmarks
beats.summary: Continual learning, long web search, robot control and SAST-versus-agent security coverage get their own evals.

beats.headline: Policy optimization and critics for sparse, long-horizon rewards
Memory, harnesses and learned orchestration for agent teams
beats.summary: Papers on self-evolving teams, memory governance, harness design and runtime-checked orchestration.

beats.headline: Retrieval and memory become the agent's context layer
beats.summary: Practitioner posts and papers treat what an agent retrieves, stores and expires as an engineering surface of its own.

beats.headline: Mistral Large 4 lands on Hugging Face with day-0 vLLM support
beats.summary: A model release swept into the cluster by its name, with a price comparison alongside.

beats.headline: Loosely linked: model internals, surveys and other side papers
beats.summary: These items share the phrase "large language models" with the thread but are not about evaluating or building agents.

beats.headline: The evals themselves come under scrutiny
beats.summary: Depth, language coverage, translated test sets, judge drift and run-to-run variance all challenge what a single score means.

beats.headline: Benchmarks target operator work: infra tuning, orchestration, code retrieval
beats.summary: JioHotstar's in-house comparison of code-retrieval approaches joins Infrathon and WorkflowArena.

open_questions: Will other benchmark authors adopt a depth measure beyond turns needed to pass a task?
Will multi-run Monte Carlo reporting become standard in agent benchmark releases?
Do results on τ-bench-LILT show a measurable gap between English and other languages for tool-using agents?
How do frontier agents score on Infrathon's infrastructure optimization tasks compared with human baselines?
Does WorkflowArena show multi-agent orchestration beating a single agent on the same tasks?
Do other teams reproduce JioHotstar's result that structural code search does well on concrete coding-agent tasks?
take_for_builders: Benchmark your coding agent's retrieval layer on your own repository tasks before choosing structural or semantic search, and run each eval several times so you report the spread, not one score.
